title: Painting is what you see: earlier strokes never redraw, flicker or swap to a sharper copy
goal: While drawing, every earlier stroke visibly recomputes: the strokes change, then swap into a higher resolution version. That looks awkward and wastes time. Painting should be what you see is what you get: the stroke you are drawing looks exactly like it will when you let go, nothing already on the canvas repaints, flickers or changes sharpness, and the whole thing answers immediately.
notes: User, 2026-10-25: 'when I draw, it seems like all of the previous strokes are recomputed because they change and then swap into this higher resolution. Seems quite awkward and inefficient at the same time. Ideally wysiwyg, and there is not flickering or repainting. but also it needs to be extremely efficient and fast, drawing can't work without immediate responsiveness'. Not reproduced in the intake window; read from code only: DocumentRenderer.raster(for:size:variant:rasterize:) (Sources/PhotonzRender/DocumentRenderer.swift:339) caches a paint layer's bitmap keyed by its WHOLE content, so one new stroke misses the cache and PaintRasterizer re-paints every stroke (the 2026-10-25 smudge sample, queue/audits/2026-10-25-smudge-freeze-sample.txt, caught exactly that). At zoom above 1, EditorState.refreshCrispTile (Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift:5592) drops the crisp tile on a change and builds a new one later, which would be the swap to a sharper copy. This is likely the shared root of every-brush-follows-the-pointer-with-no-lag-even and smudging-after-a-few-paint-strokes-never-freezes: whichever runs first writes what it changed into the others' logs, and none of them undoes another.
acceptance: Reproduce first in the probe at Next defaults: paint 5 strokes (watercolour, oil and one dry medium), then a 6th, zoomed out, at 100% and zoomed in. Record a video or frame sequence of the canvas from pointer down to a second after letting go, and MEASURE: how many earlier strokes are simulated again per new stroke, how many frames the earlier strokes differ from their settled pixels (the visible change and the swap to a sharper copy), and the time from letting go until the canvas is settled. All in the audit before any change.

After the fix, MEASURED the same way: adding a stroke simulates no earlier stroke again (a finished stroke is painted once onto a kept layer bitmap, and later strokes paint on top of it, except where watercolour genuinely needs the wet washes under it); across the whole recording, the pixels of earlier strokes outside the new stroke's reach differ from their settled values in 0 frames; the live stroke and the settled stroke match pixel for pixel or within a stated tolerance at the moment of letting go; there is no low-resolution stage at any zoom.
Immediate response holds at the same time: each drag event shows within one 120 Hz frame at p95 at 20 to 500 pt, on a layer with 50 strokes already on it, measured.

Undo, redo, opening a saved file and changing a stroke's settings still give exactly the same picture as today (pixel compare in tests); the document still keeps strokes, not baked pixels, and any kept bitmap is a cache that can always be rebuilt from them.
Memory stays bounded: the kept bitmaps have a limit and let go under memory pressure; the audit states the cost for a 12 megapixel canvas.
Logic in PhotonzRender is test-first; rendering changes carry the perf note.
A playtest walk paints six strokes and fails if any earlier stroke's pixels change while the sixth is drawn and settled.

Try path: Next defaults, Brush tool, paint several watercolour and oil strokes zoomed in to 200%, then keep drawing; nothing already painted moves, flickers or sharpens, and the new stroke looks the same before and after letting go.

An audit under queue/audits/ with the before and after recordings; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

On a 12 megapixel picture whose paint layer already holds a few hundred strokes, letting go of a stroke holds the app under 50 ms, and undoing that stroke is as quick (folded in from the dropped 12 megapixel task; the 2026-10-25 watercolour and pencil walks measured 315 to 432 ms per landing on a 4000 by 3000 canvas)
Those numbers are held by a perf test, so a later change that slows landing or undo fails the suite

The end of a mouse stroke no longer changes when the button comes up: today the pen-pressure slice draws the tail in to a point only on landing (2026-10-25-pen-pressure-tilt-and-speed audit, 0.13% of the canvas changing at release), which is exactly the held-then-landed change this task removes. Either the live stroke shows the taper as it goes, or the audit shows why that cannot work and the user picks on a card

log.note: User, 2026-10-25 (after the smudge fix d2efecfb landed): 'brushes are slow. at first its fine, after 3 or 4 large strokes it gets progressively worse perf. it needs to be constant and fast'. So the cost per drag GROWS with the number of strokes already on the layer. The bar for this task: per-drag time at stroke 1, 5, 10 and 50 (large brush) is MEASURED and stays flat, the 50th no slower than the 1st beyond noise, as well as inside the 8 ms p95. Suspects to measure, not assume: the live stroke reading every earlier wet wash (Watercolour under()/WetWash per pixel), a whole-layer re-rasterize per stroke, the overlay bitmap growing.

Its own logs: landing replays the whole layer for 344-432 ms on 4000x3000 (watercolour-wash-and-bloom-walk, pencil-draws-and-shades-walk); a landed paint layer bakes at ~1.15 px/pt on 4000x3000 while the live overlay draws at screen resolution, so at displayZoom 172 the settled stroke is softer than the held one (oil-paint-smears-and-ridges-walk with 8 zoomIn steps). Its remaining acceptance (landing and undo under 50 ms, perf test) is added here.

That is a visible change at the moment of letting go, against this task's ask that the stroke looks the same before and after. Added as an acceptance item.

User, 2026-10-26 intake: 'brushes are kind of broken perf wise after a few strokes'. Same complaint as this task (cost grows with the strokes already on the layer); moved to the front of the queue because the user wants features before test and walk work.

Reproduced before any change (walk films, 1x, 1600x1000 and 4000x3000): at 200% earlier strokes changed in 7 frames after the release (up to 46,481 px, the stretched composite showing until the sharp copy came 66 ms later), 9 strokes re-simulated per landing on the small canvas, held vs landed apart over 8 to 28% of the stroke. Causes: live stroke marked in view pixels over a redrawn copy of the layer (different pixel grid), overlay taken down with the composite while the sharp copy was also taken down and redrawn after 90 ms, the land-time taper, and a wet wash replaying earlier strokes per press.

Adversarial review before building: a Photoshop user expects the stroke to be the pixels it leaves, at any zoom; the risk was that painting the live stroke at the layer's scale costs more pixels when zoomed out (accepted: it is what makes it land unchanged). Chose painting the live stroke onto the kept raster at the shown scale over adopting the live bitmap into the cache because the cache simulating the one new stroke keeps undo/open exactness without trusting the live path, and the overlay hides the wait. Chose a live taper (tail drawn as if ending now, taken back) over a card because the media's state turned out small and uniform; tests prove held == landed per medium.

After (painting-holds-still-walk, 2x film): 0 frames change outside the new stroke at 50%, 100% and 200%; 1 stroke simulated per shown scale; at the release the picture matches the settled one over all but 0.13% of the stroke at 100% (no resampling); where the screen resamples, a one-pixel fringe can shift (stated tolerance, in the audit). Landing with 300 strokes on 12 MP holds main <= 24 ms, undo <= 9.6 ms (PaintLandingCostTests holds the shape). PaintKeepsItsPixelsTests: same pixels byte for byte as the code before.

Left open (why the task stays pending): one 120 Hz frame at p95 with a 500 pt brush. 12 MP, 50 strokes, hand pace: 20 pt every medium 2.6-7.1 ms; 500 pt marker 7.5, first wash 7.8, wash over wet washes 12.7-15.8 (was 86-112), pencil 13.6, charcoal 16.9, oil 20.6. Next: the dry media's tip loop and oil's lay are now the cost (already banded); the live tail re-marks about two dabs per new dab at 500 pt; charcoal's drag(at:) runs on one core. Measure with a walk of 50 strokes then 500 pt strokes moving 10 pt per event (a hand's pace).

left rough: the probe's film frames show faint lines where the overlay's 256 px pieces meet; real window captures held mid-stroke (100% on 12 MP, 200% on 1600x1000) show none (a real seam did exist and was fixed by hard piece edges). Did not earn a task: probe drawing only.

left rough: the brush chooser walks fail to press a tile; owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26 (logged there). With the presses swapped for pickBrush, every brush walk passes on this build, landsAsHeld checks included.

WYSIWYG painting shipped (b44c1d8b): live stroke in the layer's pixels, no frame changes earlier strokes at any zoom, live end taper, landing/undo on 12 MP with 300 strokes <= 24 / 9.6 ms, same pixels as before.
